why: A route's layout and template chains are discovered twice. `layout_chain()`
and `template_chain()` in crates/ruvyxa_graph/src/lib.rs answer for
`ruvyxa build`, and `collectLayouts()`/`collectTemplates()` in
packages/ruvyxa/runtime/compiler.mjs answer for `ruvyxa dev` and for every
route a deployed function composes. A layout one host wraps a page in and
the other does not is a page that has its `<html>`/`<body>` shell in
production and loses it locally, or the reverse.
Both halves used to pass one literal `layout.tsx` / `template.tsx` to their
nested walk, while the same two files accept `page.jsx` as a route and
accept both `default.tsx` and `default.jsx` for a slot. A project written
in `.jsx` therefore lost *every* layout and template, in both hosts, with
no diagnostic and a successful build. They were consistently wrong, which
is why nothing here failed; this table is what makes them consistently
right.
Probe order is part of the contract, not an implementation detail. `.tsx`
is probed first at every level, so a project holding a stray `layout.jsx`
beside its `layout.tsx` composes the same file it composed before `.jsx`
was accepted here at all.
`tree` lists files to create under the app directory; every one is written
with placeholder contents. `routeDir` is the directory of the route being
resolved, relative to the app directory (empty string for the root route).
`layouts` and `templates` are the expected chains in composition order —
root first — as paths relative to the app directory.
Every implementation replays this file:
- crates/ruvyxa_graph/src/lib.rs (route_chains_match_the_shared_conformance_table)
- tests/packages/ruvyxa/route-chain-contract.test.mjs
The Rust half asserts one thing the JavaScript half cannot: a chain entry
is an id with the extension stripped (`app/layout`), so the id alone does
not say which file it came from. `resolve_layout_file()` has to probe the
same extensions the chain walk did, or the chain names a layout that
nothing can load — which leaves the layout's own imports unstaged into
`<out>/server/` and the route stuck on SSR. Every case here is resolved
back to its file on that side.

cases.name: a TypeScript layout and template are found at the root
a JSX-only project keeps its layouts and templates
a JSX layout nests under a TypeScript one
tsx wins over a stray jsx at the same level
a project with neither carries empty chains
